topic: The Microscope: History, Types, Parts and Functions
key_concepts: A microscope is a tool that makes tiny objects like cells look bigger.
Most cells are too small to be seen with the naked eye.
The cell is the basic unit of structure and function of living things.
Hans and Zacharias Janssen created the first compound microscope in the 1590s.
Robert Hooke observed cork pores and named them cells in 1665.
Anton van Leeuwenhoek used a simple microscope to observe bacteria and other tiny objects.
A compound microscope has more than one lens.
The eyepiece and objective lenses magnify the image.
Total magnification equals eyepiece magnification multiplied by objective magnification.
The mirror reflects light to illuminate the specimen.
Specimens must be thin so light can pass through them.
Magnification and resolution determine how clearly a small object can be viewed.
